# ACAP Display Project

A wireless digital announcement system developed to assist and streamline the **ACAP (Against CAP) admission process** at VESIT.

The system replaces repeated manual calling-out of student names with a centralized web-based display system. Admission staff operate the system from a laptop, while two Raspberry Pi-connected displays show the selected student's information in real time.

> **Project Type:** Software Project  
> **Deployment:** ACAP Admission Process, VESIT  
> **Deployment Period:** 10 September 2026 – 15 September 2026  
> **Location:** Back Entrance, VESIT  
> **Academic Year:** 2026–27

---

## 📸 Real-World Deployment

The system was deployed in the actual ACAP admission environment rather than being limited to a prototype demonstration.

![ACAP Display Project deployed during the admission process](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

*Figure: Two ceiling-mounted displays showing the selected student's information during the ACAP admission process.*

The two displays were installed at elevated positions on beams so that students and parents could view the announcement from different areas of the admission venue.

---

## 🎯 Objective

The primary objective of the project was to **assist the ACAP admission process by displaying the merit number and names of students**, reducing the manual effort required from admission staff.

During admissions, staff traditionally had to repeatedly call out student names. In a crowded environment this could be difficult for students to hear and physically demanding for the staff.

The project provides a centralized digital alternative:

```text
Admission Staff
      │
      ▼
   Laptop
      │
      ▼
 FastAPI Web Server
      │
      │ WebSocket
      ▼
 ┌───────────────┐
 │ Local Wi-Fi   │
 └───────┬───────┘
         │
    ┌────┴────┐
    ▼         ▼
Raspberry Pi Raspberry Pi
    │         │
    ▼         ▼
Display 1   Display 2
```

---

## 🧩 System Overview

The complete system consists of:

- **1 Laptop** — hosts the FastAPI server and provides the staff control interface.
- **2 Raspberry Pis** — act as display controllers and receive information through WebSockets.
- **2 Displays** — mounted at elevated positions in the admission area.
- **Wi-Fi Dongle** — used with one Raspberry Pi that did not have built-in wireless connectivity.
- **Local Wi-Fi Network** — provides communication between the laptop/server and Raspberry Pis.

The system follows this overall flow:

```text
Excel Sheet
    ↓
FastAPI Server
    ↓
Staff Web Interface
    ↓
Student Selection
    ↓
WebSocket
    ↓
Raspberry Pis
    ↓
Displays
```

---

## ⚙️ How It Works

### 1. Connect to the local network

Admission staff connect the laptop to the designated local Wi-Fi network.

### 2. Open the web interface

The laptop accesses the web interface hosted by the FastAPI server.

### 3. Upload admission data

The student admission data is provided to the system through an Excel sheet.

### 4. Process the data

The FastAPI server processes the uploaded spreadsheet and makes the available student information accessible through the web interface.

### 5. Select a student

Admission staff select the student whose information needs to be displayed.

### 6. Transmit the selection

The selected information is sent from the server to the Raspberry Pis using a WebSocket connection.

### 7. Update both displays

Both Raspberry Pis receive the update and refresh their connected displays.

### 8. Student sees the announcement

The selected student's information becomes visible across the admission area.

## 🚀 Real-World Deployment

Unlike a purely experimental prototype, the ACAP Display Project was deployed during the actual admission process from **10 September to 15 September 2026**.

The displays were installed at elevated positions on beams within the admission area. This placement provided visibility to students and parents from different areas of the venue.

The deployment demonstrated that the system could be used as a practical centralized announcement platform in a real admission environment.

### Impact

The system helped:

- Reduce the need for staff to repeatedly shout student names.
- Make student announcements easier to see in a crowded environment.
- Provide simultaneous information across two different display locations.
- Reduce the physical effort on admission staff.
- Create a more organized experience for students, parents and staff.

---

## 💡 Why Raspberry Pi?

Raspberry Pis were used as the display controllers because the display units only needed to receive information from the central server and render it on a screen.

This keeps the display-side hardware relatively simple:

```text
Server-side processing
        ↓
      Laptop
        ↓
   Wi-Fi / WebSocket
        ↓
 Raspberry Pi
        ↓
     Display
```

The Raspberry Pis therefore act as lightweight endpoints rather than requiring the full admission-data processing system to run on each display.

---

## 🔄 Real-Time Communication

WebSockets are used for communication between the FastAPI server and Raspberry Pi clients.

This allows a selected student to be transmitted to the connected displays without requiring the operator to manually refresh the display.

```text
Staff selects student
        ↓
FastAPI server
        ↓
WebSocket message
        ↓
┌───────────────┬───────────────┐
│               │               │
▼               ▼
Pi #1           Pi #2
│               │
▼               ▼
Display 1       Display 2
```

## ▶️ Basic Working Sequence

```text
1. Start the FastAPI server
        ↓
2. Connect Raspberry Pis to local Wi-Fi
        ↓
3. Open the display clients
        ↓
4. Open the staff web interface
        ↓
5. Upload the Excel sheet
        ↓
6. Browse/select the required student
        ↓
7. Send the selection
        ↓
8. FastAPI broadcasts the update
        ↓
9. Both Raspberry Pis update
        ↓
10. Student information appears on both displays
```

---

## 🏁 Conclusion

The ACAP Display Project transformed a manual and physically demanding part of the ACAP admission process into a centralized digital display system.

By combining a FastAPI web application, WebSocket communication, Raspberry Pis and network-connected displays, admission staff were able to control multiple displays from a single laptop.

The successful deployment from **10 September to 15 September 2026** demonstrated that the system was technically functional as well as practically useful in an actual college environment.

The project improved the visibility of student announcements, reduced the need for repeated verbal announcements, and provided a more organized experience for students, parents and admission staff.
